decisions.evidence: Verified all four proof steps against the discrete, compact, compact-open, pointwise, product and subspace definitions. Pre/post diff changes only the EW locator; this is precise bibliographic enrichment, not closure of a routed defect. Dikranjan Example 7.1(2), p. 46 identifies the product topology; EW C.7, p. 434 supplies only the compact/discrete result. No item edit needed.

Preimage/raw pre hash recovered from reader log. Accepted replacing the real-only composition supplier by lem-continuity-is-local-and-pastes clause 1 and adding cor-heine-borel-in-the-product-topology clause 1. Reviewed all ten steps: epsilon factors continuously through the quotient, is bijective using [0,1) and [0,2pi), then is a compact-to-Hausdorff homeomorphism. Source correction agrees with Loomis introduction and 34D, pp. 134-135,137-138.

Definition body is byte-for-byte unchanged from the recovered preimage: continuous homomorphisms to multiplicative T, pointwise operations, compact-open subbasis and evaluation. Added justified_by makes the existing well-definedness delegation explicit; the supplier depends on this definition. Loomis 34 introduction/C/D now identifies the correct sections. These are metadata normalization; no routed finding closes here.

All five proof steps and current trigonometric/integer-part interfaces checked. The recovered preimage wrongly attributes the arc argument to Loomis 34B-D, whose complete relevant text discusses the dual topology and group structure. Accepted the corrected background/local-proof distinction. Dikranjan Example 7.1 and Theorem 7.2(a), pp. 46-47 support the no-small-subgroup property (its additive arc is larger than this arc).

Reviewed all eight proof steps and exact lifting, convexity, local-path-connectedness, connected-image and Cauchy interfaces. The based map epsilon^{-1}phi has simply connected real-line source, so lifts through p with theta(0)=0; its integer-valued additive defect is continuous and therefore constant zero. Accepted general composition citation repair and corrected source descriptions: EW C.14(2), p. 438 and Dikranjan Example 7.7 state the result, not this covering-space proof; Loomis 35C uses a different argument.

Accepted reader correction of the false equality in step 3.1 by restoring the modulus-one factor gamma(x-x0), and the use of open V in step 4.1. Compact closure can be chosen inside the continuity neighbourhood by the exact locally-compact-Hausdorff shrinking lemma. Loomis 34A pp. 135-136 does state joint continuity through the maximal-ideal representation, and 34C identifies its topology; an initial citation suspicion was rejected after reading the complete passage. No additional carrier edit.

Accepted replacing ill-typed S(K,B(f,r)) by defined uniform neighbourhoods U_K(f,r). Read all seven steps: finite compact patches prove these sets open, a maximum-error margin proves openness at every member, and finite target-ball covers prove refinement of the compact-open subbasis. Both inclusions of the topology comparison hold for an arbitrary abelian topological domain, including non-Hausdorff domains. Exact compact-image, finite-union, closed-compact and ambient-cover suppliers checked. Loomis 34C-D supplies the uniform-operation estimate for LCA groups; the arbitrary-domain extension is proved locally.

Read all five steps and the full pointwise-closure-preserves-equicontinuity supplier. Closedness is the intersection of closed homomorphism equations in T^G; continuity of limits requires the stated equicontinuous family. Accepted qualification of the title, explicit group/domain hypotheses, multiplication in F1, general composition citation and correct Loomis background attribution. Direct consumers are the compact/discrete theorem using clause (3), and the compact-identity lemma using clause (2) after establishing equicontinuity; both hypotheses are preserved. A-page prose now includes equicontinuity. No outside consumer found.

Reviewed all eight steps, quotient/open-map interfaces and exact AC use. Preimages of compact-open subbasic sets are S(phi[K],V), proving continuity and contravariant functoriality. Closed H gives a Hausdorff locally compact topological quotient; annihilator closedness and factorization are correct. The local compact-lift proof produces K with L contained in q[K], which suffices for inverse continuity. Accepted general-composition repair and Dikranjan locator correction to Lemma 7.16 and Corollary 7.29 (read complete relevant proofs); EW C.13 and Loomis 35B support quotient duality.

Reviewed all seven steps, full Ascoli/equicontinuity supplier proofs, FIP and net interfaces. Descending closed power constraints in compact T eventually lie in every identity ball; pulling back the finitely many constraints through u->ju makes N equicontinuous. N is closed in C(G,T), and its compact-open closure is compact under the declared Choice hypothesis. Accepted general composition correction and corrected source scope: Dikranjan 7.2(f2)-(f3) states compact closure, not compactness of its original open constraint; Loomis 34D does not give this local Ascoli proof.

All five steps checked. The compact case isolates the identity by S(G,D), then translates; the discrete case is the closed homomorphism subspace of compact T^G, using declared AC through Tychonoff. Reader corrected the unsupported Loomis locator. Adjudicator additionally corrected the remaining EW C.7 attribution: its pp. 434-435 proof uses Fourier orthogonality, not a product embedding. The local product proof agrees with Dikranjan Example 7.1(2), p. 46. Item edit is only the source locator; mathematical statement/proof and all consumers remain unchanged.

Read all seven steps and finite product/direct sum/compactness interfaces. Accepted the F1 general-composition citation repair. Finite-product characters split by coordinate restrictions, and both topology directions use compact projections and compact boxes containing coordinate axes. For a discrete algebraic direct sum the finite-support formula is a bijection; coordinate pullbacks give continuity and compact-to-Hausdorff gives the inverse under Choice. Dikranjan Lemma 7.12 and Theorem 7.14, pp. 50-51, and Loomis 35A give these results. No claim for non-discrete direct sums.

Read all four steps. Accepted adding 1 in V to the displayed identity-neighbourhood family: the preimage statement incorrectly included target opens missing 1, which yield empty sets for nonempty K. The proof already used identity-containing opens. A finite subbasic intersection is refined by a finite compact union and finite target-open intersection (discard empty compact tests); a symmetric compact neighbourhood gives the proved compact N_K, then translations give local compactness. Accepted general-composition citation repair. EW C.6, Dikranjan 7.2(f3), and Loomis 34D state local compactness. Consumer search finds only the owned A-page; its LCA summary is sound.

All four verification steps checked against the presented residue group, roots-of-unity and integer power interfaces. Accepted explicit exponential-addition citation/derivation in F4 and source corrections: Dikranjan Proposition 7.13 proof, p. 51 gives finite cyclic duals; Loomis 35C concerns the line, and current 35D-E citations are explicitly background. Classification and topology are unchanged.

All six steps checked. The real-line composite is chi epsilon p, not chi epsilon; classification yields xi, periodicity at k=1 forces xi integer, and surjectivity of epsilon gives the power map on T. Accepted the F5 typing correction, explicit exponential integer-power derivation and general composition supplier. Source repairs now match EW p. 436 and Loomis 35D p. 140, with Dikranjan Lemma 7.5/Example 7.7 pp. 48-49. Adjudicator corrected the remaining equation locator from (C.3) to (C.2), and limited the p. 436 claim to the circle; that passage contains no finite-torus classification.

Reviewed all five verification steps and integer/complex-power interfaces. Evaluation at 1 gives the inverse; a character is z^n by induction and inverse preservation. The parameter map is continuous into T^Z coordinatewise for positive, zero and negative powers; pointwise equals compact-open on discrete Z. Accepted general-composition supplier repair and corrected source locator from Loomis 35C to 35E p. 140, consistent with Dikranjan Example 7.7 and EW C.14(1).

Reviewed all six verification steps and exact norm/Cauchy-Schwarz/product-topology interfaces. Accepted the empty-K branch and nonempty maximum hypothesis, explicit character well-definedness, Cauchy-Schwarz supplier, Euclidean/product compatibility, and general composition. Forward continuity uses delta'=tolerance and delta'/(R+1); inverse continuity tests x0=eta/(2||eta||^2) in a closed ball and obtains phase 1/2. Reader corrected Loomis to 35C plus 35A. Adjudicator additionally narrowed the Dikranjan locator: Example 7.7 p. 49 computes the line, while Lemma 7.12 p. 50 supplies finite products; the Euclidean computation is their consequence.

Confirmed the current unedited preimage at summary lines 21-23: chi epsilon has circle source and need not lift through R->T. For chi=id, a hypothetical lift ell makes a(t)=ell([t]) continuous with a(t)-t integer-valued, hence constant on connected R, while a(1)=a(0), a contradiction. The actual circle item correctly precomposes with p:R->R/Z. Repaired only this sentence to precompose chi with t->exp(2pi it), apply the line classification, then use periodicity to force integer frequency. This retains the classification, topology, placement and Choice disclosure. Remaining summary checked against all four reviewed computations.
